_fixture_metadata.source: real deepseek-chat API, mode=deepseek, plan_semantic_analysis tool call
_fixture_metadata.question: In ADNI, what are the mean cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) p-tau181 levels for Cognitively Normal (CN), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer's Disease (AD) groups at baseline?
_fixture_metadata.observed_bug: CN/MCI/AD all compiled to filter={} -> eligible_n=3711 (unfiltered) for all three; grounded=True, question_answered=True, semantic_grounding_passed=True despite the defect
_fixture_metadata.root_cause: each group's baseline_filters uses raw ADNI column names with operator objects (e.g. {'DXMCI': 1, 'DXAD': {'neq': 1}}) instead of the expected {'diagnosis': '<label>'} shape -- _filter_dict_for_scope() only ever reads the literal key 'diagnosis', silently ignoring everything else. C14 compared these raw dicts (which are NOT byte-identical to each other) so it never fired; the identical failure only appears in the COMPILED filter, one boundary later.

raw_plan_data.outcome_definition: N/A — this is a cross-sectional baseline comparison, not an outcome prediction
raw_plan_data.denominator_definition: For each group defined below (CN, MCI, AD), the denominator is the unique ADNI participants in that diagnostic group at their baseline (first) visit who have a non-missing CSF p-tau181 value (raw or harmonized) at that same visit.
known_invalid_interpretations: NOT a count of visit rows — population_unit is participant
NOT any-visit or longitudinal analysis — cohort_scope is baseline only
NOT using NACCUDSD or NACCALZD (those are Space A NACC variables, not applicable for ADNI)
NOT including participants who converted later — baseline diagnosis only
NOT a single pooled mean across all groups — groups are separate CN, MCI, AD
caveats: The question says CSF p-tau181 levels. The catalog has two matching variables in the ptau181 family: ADNI.ADSP_PHC_CSF.PHC_pTau181 (csf_harmonized, harmonized Z-score) and ADNI.ADSP_PHC_CSF.pTau181_RAW (csf_raw, raw levels). Both measure CSF p-tau181 but are on different scales. The question does not specify raw vs. harmonized, so both variants should be reported separately.

The group label 'AD' is ambiguous: it could mean a clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (syndromic, as captured by DXAD=1) or it could imply etiologic AD (which ADNI does not use NACCALZD for). Since the catalog provides ADNI.DXSUM.DXAD (1=Yes) for AD diagnosis, and ADNI.DXSUM.DXMCI (1=Yes) for MCI, and CN is the absence of both, we interpret 'AD' as the syndromic clinical diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease per ADNI DXAD=1.
